trust_decision.summary: A document-supplied hyperlink target (and a font name / attachment data URL) is untrusted and must not reach an anchor href or a style attribute as an executable scheme; the decision is enforced in @file-viewer/doc's HTML builder and again at every DOM mount, including the separate @file-viewer/renderer-word mount.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'DOM XSS via unsafe hyperlink schemes in the legacy DOC renderer', so the first stop is the msdoc-link anchor template in the doc package's HTML renderer, where node.href is interpolated after escapeHtml only.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names '@file-viewer/doc's legacy DOC renderer'; @file-viewer/renderer-word is a separate package whose HTML comes from parseMsDocToHtml, which the report's own fix already scheme-checks at the string boundary, so a solver can argue the wrapper's own target.innerHTML needs no second, DOM-level sanitizer.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Embedded attachment download links built from data:application/octet-stream;base64 URLs, and internal bookmark anchors (#bookmark), must stay clickable next to the blocked data:text/html and javascript: values; a blanket 'drop every href / reject every data: URL' fix breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: control-character-obfuscated scheme, e.g. 'JaVa\nScRiPt:...' (normalised before the scheme test)
plain dangerous schemes: javascript:, vbscript:, file:, blob:
data: URIs used as hrefs, including data:text/html and data:image/svg+xml
allow-listed schemes https:, http:, mailto:, tel:, plus #bookmark anchors
data: download URLs with an allow-listed MIME (application/octet-stream;base64) versus text/html, image/svg+xml, application/xhtml+xml and any +xml suffix
font-family strings that break out of the quoted CSS string into a new attribute
arbitrary HTML with event-handler attributes handed to the DOM mount

O7_producer.where: packages/renderers/doc/src/msdoc/parser.ts:64-73 (decodeFieldInstruction HYPERLINK -> href), applied to inline nodes at packages/renderers/doc/src/msdoc/parser.ts:278-284

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second DOC DOM mount (export/print or thumbnail path) that re-inserts rendered.html without going through mountMsDoc
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same file already hands DOC DOM/HTML to other consumers via the export clone (packages/renderers/word/src/wordDoc.ts:203-239) and the thumbnail adapter (packages/renderers/word/src/wordDoc.ts:439-441), so a maintainer adding one more mount is in character.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third attachment/object list renderer (embedded OLE objects or icon table) with its own href template
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the package already carries two parallel attachment paths - inline attachment nodes (packages/renderers/doc/src/render/html.ts:268-275) and the attachments block (packages/renderers/doc/src/render/html.ts:377-380) - and the published fix had to change both.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a DOCX-style post-mount anchor policy (applyDocxExternalLinkPolicy) mirrored as a DOC-level DOM pass instead of a render-time check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: that helper already exists in the same package (packages/renderers/word/src/wordDocx.ts:380-403) and the published fix reuses its option name, reading context?.options?.docx?.externalLinkPolicy (fix.diff:3201), so a maintainer could plausibly enforce the DOC policy the same post-mount way.

O9_family: DOM-based XSS via unsafe hyperlink schemes and CSS/attribute injection (CWE-79, CWE-83)

O10_build.project_tests: packages/renderers/doc: tsc build plus node verify scripts verify:table-spec / verify:github-34 / -87 / -171 / -192 and test/browser-table-smoke.ts (fixture-driven, browser); repo-level `pnpm verify:renderer-sanitization` (package.json:41) = apps/viewer-demo/scripts/verify-renderer-sanitization.mjs, headless Chromium, which at the pinned commit covers markdown and pptx only (apps/viewer-demo/scripts/verify-renderer-sanitization.mjs:488)
